evidence_chain: FACT: WEST's 2025 Form 10-K states that scaling and commercializing customers at the Conway facility is a material execution risk, implying the facility is central to the company thesis and still in ramp-verification mode. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1806347/000110465926025932/west-20251231x10k.htm

FACT: The 2025 10-K revenue disclosure indicates that no customer accounted for more than 10% of consolidated net revenues in 2025 or 2024, while one Beverage Solutions customer exceeded 10% in 2023. This supports lower disclosed concentration at the consolidated level but does not prove high-quality diversification inside the most important growth lines. Source: https://app.edgar.tools/companies/WEST/disclosures/revenue

FACT: WEST reported Q1 2026 net sales of $308.8 million, up 44.4% year over year; gross profit of $45.8 million, up 57.4%; net loss of $8.5 million versus a $27.2 million loss in the prior-year period; and consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $26.0 million. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WEST/westrock-coffee-company-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-and-i0yhjkxi7hna.html

FACT: Q1 2026 external earnings materials report that all five production lines at the Conway extract and RTD facility were fully commercialized and that the company reaffirmed 2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance of $90.0 million to $100.0 million. Source: https://investors.westrockcoffee.com/node/9141/pdf

FACT: The Q1 2026 earnings transcript describes the Conway facility as fully operational with all five lines active and operating cash-flow positive, while also describing active commercial work across tea, lemonade-based refreshers, coffee RTD beverages, packaged coffee, single-serve cups, energy drinks, high-protein drinks, and seltzers. Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/westrock-coffee-west-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/

FACT: WEST's FY2025 release reported consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $69.7 million and $15.3 million of Conway facility scale-up costs, compared with adjusted EBITDA of $47.2 million and $12.8 million of Conway scale-up costs in the prior year. Source: https://westrockcoffee.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/westrock-coffee-company-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-1

INFERENCE: The combination of Q1 2026 revenue growth, gross-profit growth, adjusted EBITDA improvement, and full Conway commercialization suggests an operational inflection, but it does not yet prove durable free-cash-flow generation or customer lock-in.
HYPOTHESIS: If Conway utilization rises under recurring contracts with pass-through pricing, WEST's economics could shift from scale-up losses toward manufacturing operating leverage.

HYPOTHESIS: If the main Q1 2026 improvement came from temporary mix, one-time contract benefits, inventory timing, or commodity lag rather than recurring manufacturing margin, the chokepoint thesis should be downgraded.
falsification_plan: Downgrade the thesis if Q2 or Q3 2026 shows Conway utilization ramping slower than management commentary implies, or if incremental revenue requires price concessions that prevent gross-margin expansion.
Downgrade the thesis if Beverage Solutions adjusted EBITDA growth stalls after excluding one-time contract benefits, commodity timing, and scale-up cost normalization.
Downgrade the thesis if new customer programs do not replace lost or declining volumes within the stated timeline.
Downgrade the thesis if gross margin compresses during coffee-cost volatility, indicating weak pass-through protection or unfavorable pricing lags.
Downgrade the thesis if capex falls but free cash flow remains materially negative without a clear working-capital explanation.
Downgrade the thesis if secured leverage, preferred-share obligations, or covenant constraints create a credible need for dilutive financing.
Downgrade the thesis if customer concentration disclosures worsen, or if a major undisclosed customer category appears to be driving most of the Conway ramp without durable contract protection.

Upgrade the thesis only if filings or calls show rising contracted utilization, recurring gross-margin expansion, lower scale-up costs, customer diversification, and credible free-cash-flow inflection.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The key hidden signal is contracted utilization of Conway capacity by restaurant chains, convenience-store systems, hospitality customers, CPG brands, and private-label programs. Specific indicators to verify are: named or described customer categories, committed capacity, take-or-pay or minimum-volume terms, line-level utilization, gross-margin pass-through formulas for green coffee and inputs, customer onboarding timing, repeat program launches, and evidence that Conway shortens sales cycles because customers value installed RTD and extract capacity.

Pull the Q1 2026 10-Q when available and compare operating cash flow, working capital, capex, debt, covenant headroom, and segment margin against management's adjusted EBITDA narrative.

Build a bridge from FY2025 adjusted EBITDA to 2026 guidance: remove Conway scale-up costs, identify one-time contract benefits, estimate recurring segment EBITDA, and test whether $90 million to $100 million is achievable without heroic assumptions.
Map WEST's customer end-markets into restaurant, convenience store, hospitality, CPG, private label, and retail. Mark all claims as fact only if disclosed in filings, presentations, or calls.

Search for customer announcements, product launches, supplier qualification news, certifications, and plant permits connected to Conway, RTD, extracts, cold brew, tea, refreshers, energy drinks, and high-protein beverages.
Compare WEST against public or private beverage co-manufacturing peers where data is available: capacity, certifications, packaging formats, extract capability, customer types, and capex intensity.
Track commodity coffee prices versus WEST gross margin quarterly to test whether pass-through mechanisms are protecting economics.
Monitor whether capex declines after Conway completion and whether free cash flow turns positive in the second half of 2026, as suggested by external earnings context.

Create a dashboard watchlist with quarterly fields: net sales growth, Beverage Solutions revenue, gross margin, adjusted EBITDA, scale-up costs, operating cash flow, capex, free cash flow, net leverage, revolver availability, customer concentration, and Conway utilization commentary.
risks: Execution risk: Conway may be fully commercialized but still underutilized relative to its fixed-cost base; commercialization does not equal contracted high utilization.
Customer replacement risk: lost or changing single-serve, private-label, or branded customer volumes may not be replaced on the expected timeline.
Margin-quality risk: adjusted EBITDA improvement may overstate recurring economics if driven by one-time benefits, favorable timing, or temporary commodity-cost lags.
Commodity pass-through risk: green coffee and other input-cost volatility may pressure gross margin if contractual pricing formulas lag or fail.
Balance-sheet risk: leverage, preferred-share obligations, revolver availability, covenant headroom, and cash-flow timing could force financing or constrain operations before free cash flow improves.
Customer concentration opacity: consolidated disclosure below 10% does not rule out dependence on a few key customers within specific lines, categories, or facilities.
Channel risk: restaurant, convenience, retail, and branded-beverage customers can delay launches, insource production, switch co-manufacturers, or pressure pricing.
Competitive risk: other beverage co-manufacturers or large CPG-owned facilities may absorb growth if WEST cannot offer better quality, speed, cost, certifications, or scale.
Evidence risk: the current thesis relies partly on management commentary and external earnings summaries; line-level utilization, contract terms, and customer identities are not yet fully observable.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Restaurants and beverage brands -> menu innovation / private-label / RTD beverage programs -> outsourced beverage formulation, extraction, filling, packaging, and sourcing -> WEST Beverage Solutions and Sustainable Sourcing & Traceability segments -> Conway, Arkansas extract and ready-to-drink facility plus coffee / tea sourcing and packaging platform. WEST sits one or two layers upstream from consumer-facing restaurant traffic: it may benefit when chains, convenience stores, hospitality accounts, and branded beverage companies outsource beverage production rather than build dedicated capacity themselves.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：WEST 不是传统餐厅运营商，而是餐饮、便利店、零售和品牌饮料客户背后的二阶供应链平台。如果 Conway 工厂的咖啡、茶、提取物和 RTD 产线能够形成高利用率、合同锁定、成本可传导的外包制造能力，WEST 可能成为餐饮饮料菜单升级和即饮饮料扩张中的稀缺制造节点。当前事实支持 Conway 已进入商业化和业绩改善阶段；但核心仍需验证：客户是否足够优质、产能是否被长期合同吸收、毛利是否能穿越咖啡成本波动、以及杠杆压力是否不会在自由现金流转正前破坏股东价值。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: WEST is not a conventional restaurant operator; it is a second-order supply-chain platform behind restaurants, convenience stores, retail channels, and branded beverage programs. If its Conway facility turns coffee, tea, extract, and RTD lines into high-utilization, contract-backed, pass-through-protected outsourced manufacturing capacity, WEST could become a scarce production node for beverage menu innovation and ready-to-drink expansion. The current facts support a Conway commercialization and earnings-improvement inflection, but the thesis still depends on customer quality, contracted utilization, gross-margin protection, and balance-sheet survivability before free cash flow inflects.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Restaurant equity screens usually prioritize visible operators, franchisors, store-count growth, same-store sales, food distributors, or consumer coffee chains. WEST can be missed because its exposure is embedded in B2B beverage procurement, private-label programs, extracts, RTD co-manufacturing, single-serve coffee, traceable sourcing, and customer contracts rather than store openings. The hidden restaurant signal is not whether coffee prices rise or fall; it is whether large foodservice and beverage customers increasingly need outsourced, certified, scaled manufacturing capacity that can handle beverage innovation without customer-owned capex.

summary: Layer 5 mini deep report for WEST within the Restaurants theme. WEST is treated as an underfollowed, second-order beverage infrastructure candidate rather than a restaurant operator. The investable research question is whether Conway-based coffee, tea, extract, and RTD manufacturing capacity becomes a contracted, high-utilization outsourced production node for restaurant, convenience-store, retail, and branded beverage customers. Current evidence supports a real operational inflection, but the thesis remains a hypothesis because customer mix, contract duration, pass-through economics, free-cash-flow conversion, leverage, and recurring margin quality still require verification.
